is: One tick of the spawner, split into a pure planner, the run folders that record each launch and the process holding it, the counter-only .zaf/spawn.state, and the I/O that reserves launches, runs team instances through the Runner port and records them in their run folders and on the epic. Nothing it plans from is kept in step by hand: running instances, slots and live claims are derived on every read.
conventions: tick.rs stays pure (no port, no file); every side effect lives in mod.rs
Launch and exit are HTML-comment markers on the epic: `<!-- zaf:launch <instance> -->`, `<!-- zaf:exit <instance> <status> -->`

Derive, never keep in step: whether a launch runs is its run folder's pid (pid plus start time) checked against the process table on every read; only the counter, the launch record and the exit are written

fs.name: blockers.rs
fs.role: Blocked by: parsing, the blocker graph, its cycles and dead blockers

fs.name: mod.rs
fs.role: prepare (lost, orphaned claims, plan, reserve under spawn.lock), launch, launch_all, dry run

fs.name: runs.rs
fs.role: .zaf/runs/<slug>/: launch.json, the holding process in pid, exit; Run::running reads the process table

fs.name: state.rs
fs.role: .zaf/spawn.state, the instance counter alone; derive() adds the launches that run now

fs.name: tick.rs
fs.role: board snapshot, derived running launches, guard and settings in, launch plan out

notes: Only the team-instance branch is built; tick.rs names planning, challenger and release as NOT_BUILT and skips them, and the teams README says so
The verb never loops; an external timer runs `zaf spawn --once`
The launch prompt and standing brief are assets/spawn/team-prompt.txt and team-brief.md
Slots and guard thresholds come from ZAF.toml [spawn]; the guard level is read from .zaf/guard.json; a batch of tasks shares one instance and one slot
